title: Quantum error correction as syndrome measurement
confusion_guard: Syndrome measurement is a quantum operation on a declared code space. Drawing cyan ripples on a lattice plate does not demonstrate a physical self-healing vacuum.
definitions: A stabilizer group S is an abelian subgroup of the Pauli group not containing -I.
The code space is the +1 eigenspace of every element of S.
A syndrome is the tuple of measurement outcomes of a generating set of checks.
mechanism: Syndrome measurement projects the state onto a coset of the code. A classical decoder maps the syndrome to a recovery operator. For a CSS code built from G24, that classical decoder can be the Golay decoder shipped in this lab.
predictions: If all checks yield +1 and the state started in the code space, it remains there.
For a CSS code from G24, any classical weight-≤3 error on one block is in principle correctable.
assumptions: Checks commute and can be measured without leaving the code space when no error occurred.
The noise model is declared (e.g. independent Pauli errors below a threshold).
falsification_conditions: A declared stabilizer family that does not commute.
A claimed Golay CSS implementation whose measured syndrome does not match the classical parity checks of G24.

evidence.source: Gottesman, Stabilizer codes and quantum error correction
Multiple laboratory demonstrations of small stabilizer codes (surface, repetition, color) — not a Golay CSS device in this index
evidence.notes: Supports the syndrome mechanism, not a specific G24 quantum implementation here.

description: A stabilizer code detects errors by measuring commuting Pauli checks. The syndrome names a coset; a decoder proposes a recovery. Classical codes such as G24 enter as CSS ingredients — they are not themselves quantum memories.
